scenario: 面试官问「你怎么知道这个企业 RAG 问答系统能用」。有工程师想直接套 BLEU/ROUGE 分数。
scenario_en: The interviewer asks 'how do you know this enterprise RAG QA system works?' An engineer wants to just report BLEU/ROUGE scores.
q: 为什么 BLEU/ROUGE 不适合评估 RAG 系统？
q_en: Why are BLEU/ROUGE inadequate for evaluating a RAG system?
why: BLEU/ROUGE 是机器翻译的 n-gram 重叠指标，测的是「和参考答案字面像不像」，测不出幻觉、检索错误或伪造引用。而 RAG 的主要失败其实在检索不到位（检索错上下文→答案没有依据），字面重叠完全看不见这条链路。
why_en: BLEU/ROUGE only measure n-gram overlap with a reference and miss hallucination, wrong retrieval, and fabricated citations, whereas RAG's primary failure mode is inadequate retrieval.
tradeoff: 字面重叠指标（易算但盲于幻觉/检索）vs 面向 RAG 的忠实/相关/可溯源评估
whenOtherWins: 如果任务本身就是「输出要逐字贴近唯一标准答案」（如术语翻译、模板填充），n-gram 重叠反而是合适的直接指标。
options: 因为 BLEU/ROUGE 计算太慢，跑一遍要几小时，跟不上线上流量
因为它们只测 n-gram 字面重叠，盲于幻觉与检索错误
因为它们只支持英文，企业多语言合同库的问答场景无法计算
因为它们需要 GPU 推理，成本比直接用 LLM 打分还高
options_en: Because BLEU/ROUGE are too slow to compute, taking hours per run, and cannot keep up with live traffic.
Because they only measure n-gram overlap and are blind to hallucination and retrieval errors.
Because they only support English and cannot be computed for enterprise multilingual contract QA.
Because they require GPU inference and cost more than just using an LLM to score.
optionExplanations: 速度不是问题所在：BLEU/ROUGE 其实算得很快，问题是它们测的东西（字面重叠）跟 RAG 的失败模式对不上。
对；RAG 答错通常是检索错了上下文导致答案没根据，n-gram 重叠既看不出幻觉也看不出检索是否切题。
多语言不是核心缺陷，n-gram 指标各语言都能算；真正的缺陷是它衡量的维度错了。
BLEU/ROUGE 是纯字符串统计、根本不用 GPU；成本论点站不住，问题在于指标维度错位。
optionExplanations_en: Speed is not the issue: BLEU/ROUGE are actually fast; the problem is what they measure (surface overlap) does not match RAG's failure modes.
Correct — RAG errors usually come from retrieving the wrong context so the answer lacks grounding, and n-gram overlap sees neither hallucination nor retrieval relevance.
Multilingual is not the core flaw; n-gram metrics work in any language, the real flaw is they measure the wrong dimension.
BLEU/ROUGE are pure string statistics needing no GPU, so the cost argument fails; the issue is the metric measures the wrong thing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索增强生成：先检索相关文档片段，再让 LLM 基于这些片段作答。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) retrieves relevant document chunks first, then has an LLM answer grounded in those chunks.

termDefinitions.meaning: 机器翻译评测指标，衡量生成文本与参考答案的 n-gram 重叠。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BLEU (Bilingual Evaluation Understudy) is a machine-translation metric scoring n-gram overlap between output and a reference.

termDefinitions.meaning: 摘要评测指标，偏召回地衡量与参考文本的 n-gram 重叠。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: ROUGE (Recall-Oriented Understudy for Gisting Evaluation) is a summarization metric measuring recall-oriented n-gram overlap with a reference.

scenario: 评估企业 RAG 时要拆成互不重叠的几个维度，避免把不同的失败糊成一个分数。
scenario_en: Evaluating enterprise RAG means splitting into non-overlapping dimensions so different failures don't collapse into one score.
q: RAG Triad（RAG 三元评估）是哪三个维度？
q_en: What are the three dimensions of the RAG Triad?
why: 三个非冗余维度：Faithfulness（答案是否忠于检索到的上下文，抓幻觉）、Relevance（检索到的上下文是否切题，抓上游检索失败）、Groundedness（每条主张是否有引用支撑，抓无依据断言）。三者各抓一类失败，缺一漏一。
why_en: The three non-redundant dimensions are Faithfulness (does the answer reflect retrieved context, catching hallucination), Relevance (does retrieved context answer the query, catching retrieval failure), and Groundedness (is every claim backed by a cited passage).
diagram:
flowchart LR Q["用户 query"] --> R["检索 chunks"] R --> A["生成答案"] R -.Relevance.-> Q A -.Faithfulness.-> R A -.Groundedness
逐条引用.-> R
options: Accuracy、Precision、Recall——沿用分类模型的三个标准指标
Faithfulness（忠实于上下文）、Relevance（上下文切题）、Groundedness（逐条可溯源）
Latency（延迟）、Throughput（吞吐）、Cost（成本）——服务侧三件套
Fluency（流畅度）、Coherence（连贯性）、Diversity（多样性）——生成文本三指标
options_en: Accuracy, Precision, Recall — the three standard classification metrics.
Faithfulness (answer reflects context), Relevance (context answers the query), Groundedness (each claim is attributable).
Latency, Throughput, Cost — the serving-side trio.
Fluency, Coherence, Diversity — three generic text-generation metrics.
optionExplanations: 分类指标假设有单一正确标签，RAG 的开放式答案没有这种标签，也测不出检索链路的问题。
对；这三维分别盯住幻觉、检索是否切题、以及每条主张能否溯源，互不重叠地覆盖 RAG 的失败模式。
延迟/吞吐/成本是服务性能，不评估答案质量；一个又快又便宜的系统照样可能满口幻觉。
流畅/连贯/多样只看文字表面好不好读，答案再通顺也可能完全脱离检索到的事实。
optionExplanations_en: Classification metrics assume a single correct label; RAG's open-ended answers have none and reveal nothing about the retrieval path.
Correct — these three watch hallucination, retrieval relevance, and per-claim attribution, covering RAG failures without overlap.
Latency/throughput/cost are serving performance, not answer quality; a fast cheap system can still hallucinate constantly.
Fluency/coherence/diversity only judge how readable the text is; a fluent answer can still be fully detached from retrieved facts.

termDefinitions.term: RAG Triad / RAG 三元评估
termDefinitions.meaning: 用 Faithfulness、Relevance、Groundedness 三个非冗余维度评估 RAG 的框架。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The RAG Triad evaluates RAG on three non-redundant dimensions: Faithfulness, Relevance, and Groundedness.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案是否只陈述检索上下文支持的内容，用来抓幻觉。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faithfulness measures whether the answer only states what the retrieved context supports, catching hallucination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 检索回来的上下文是否真的能回答用户 query，用来抓上游检索失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Relevance measures whether the retrieved context can actually answer the query, catching upstream retrieval failure.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案里每一条主张是否都能对应到某个被引用的段落。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Groundedness measures whether every claim in the answer maps to a specific cited passage.

scenario: 有人问：既然 Faithfulness 和 Relevance 都在评估 RAG，是不是测一个就够了？
scenario_en: Someone asks: since Faithfulness and Relevance both evaluate RAG, isn't measuring one enough?
q: Faithfulness 和 Relevance 为什么是「非冗余」的两个维度？
q_en: Why are Faithfulness and Relevance non-redundant dimensions?
why: Faithfulness 看「答案 vs 上下文」，Relevance 看「上下文 vs query」。系统可以忠实复述一段无关上下文，所以两个分必须分开测。
why_en: They watch different relationships — Faithfulness is answer-versus-context and Relevance is context-versus-query — so you can be faithful to irrelevant context or ignore relevant context, and must measure both.
tradeoff: Faithfulness（答案↔上下文）vs Relevance（上下文↔query）——两条不同关系轴

rows: 忠实复述了无关上下文
检索切题却被答案忽略

options: 它们其实等价，Relevance 高必然 Faithfulness 高，测一个即可
Faithfulness 只在生成阶段有意义，Relevance 只在离线阶段有意义，两者在时间上错开互不重叠
Faithfulness 看答案是否忠于上下文，Relevance 看上下文是否切题，可忠实于无关上下文
Relevance 是主观指标、Faithfulness 是客观指标，一个靠人一个靠机器，两条尺子无法放一起比
options_en: They are actually equivalent — high Relevance implies high Faithfulness, so measure just one.
Faithfulness matters only at generation time and Relevance only offline, so they never overlap in time.
Faithfulness checks if the answer is faithful to the context, Relevance checks if the context is on-topic, and you can be faithful to irrelevant context.
Relevance is subjective and Faithfulness objective, one needs humans and one machines, so the two rulers cannot be compared.
optionExplanations: 反例直接推翻：可以检索到完全无关但被忠实复述的上下文，Relevance 低而 Faithfulness 高。
两者都在评估同一次问答的不同关系，没有时间先后之分，这个划分是编造的。
对；一个比「答案↔上下文」、一个比「上下文↔query」，两条关系轴正交，一个高不推出另一个高。
主观/客观不是它们的区别；两者都可以用 LLM 判、也都可以人工标，区别在比较的对象不同。
optionExplanations_en: A counterexample kills it: context can be totally irrelevant yet faithfully echoed — low Relevance, high Faithfulness.
Both evaluate different relationships within the same QA turn; there is no temporal ordering, this split is invented.
Correct — one compares answer-to-context, the other context-to-query; the two axes are orthogonal, so high in one need not mean high in the other.
Subjective/objective is not the distinction; both can be judged by an LLM or by humans, the difference is what they compare.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两个指标测的是不同关系，一个的高低推不出另一个，所以都要测。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Non-redundant means the two metrics measure different relationships, so one's value cannot be inferred from the other.

scenario: 合同问答系统要出审计报告，需要逐条主张都能指到具体段落，光「答案没跑偏」还不够。
scenario_en: A contract QA system must produce audit reports where every claim points to a specific passage; 'the answer didn't drift' is not enough.
q: Groundedness 比 Faithfulness 严在哪里？
q_en: How is Groundedness stricter than Faithfulness?
why: Faithfulness 只要求答案整体不与上下文矛盾；Groundedness 更严，要求「每一条主张」都能映射到某个具体段落 ID，做逐条溯源。审计场景需要 attribution（可归因），所以要用更严的 Groundedness。
why_en: Faithfulness only requires the answer not to contradict the context, while Groundedness is stricter, demanding each individual claim map to a specific passage ID for a per-claim audit trail.
tradeoff: Faithfulness（整体不矛盾即可）vs Groundedness（逐条 attribution，更严）
options: Groundedness 要求每条主张映射到具体段落 ID；Faithfulness 只要整体不矛盾
Groundedness 只看引用格式对不对，Faithfulness 才看内容对不对，前者其实更松
Groundedness 用机器判、Faithfulness 用人判，严不严只是标注成本高低的说法
两者完全相同，Groundedness 只是 Faithfulness 在多轮对话里的别名
options_en: Groundedness requires each claim to map to a specific passage ID; Faithfulness only needs the whole answer not to contradict.
Groundedness only checks citation formatting and Faithfulness checks content, so Groundedness is actually looser.
Groundedness is machine-judged and Faithfulness human-judged; strictness is just about labeling cost.
They are identical; Groundedness is just Faithfulness's alias in multi-turn dialogue.
optionExplanations: 对；粒度是关键——Groundedness 逐条把主张钉到段落上，能出审计追踪，比只看整体一致的 Faithfulness 严。
说反了；Groundedness 恰恰是内容级的逐条溯源，不是格式检查，也不比 Faithfulness 松。
严不严跟谁来判无关，两者都能机判或人判；区别在 Groundedness 的判定粒度更细（逐条）。
两者不同：一个是整体忠实，一个是逐条可归因，不是别名关系。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — granularity is the key: Groundedness pins each claim to a passage for an audit trail, stricter than Faithfulness's whole-answer consistency.
Backwards; Groundedness is content-level per-claim attribution, not a format check, and is not looser than Faithfulness.
Strictness is independent of who judges; both can be machine or human judged, the difference is Groundedness's finer per-claim granularity.
They differ: one is whole-answer faithfulness, the other per-claim attributability — not aliases.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把答案里的每条主张对应到支撑它的具体段落，用于审计追踪。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Attribution maps each claim in the answer to the specific passage supporting it, enabling an audit trail.

scenario: 法律 RAG 答案里冒出一条「合同第 7 条约定」的内容，但翻遍所有检索到的 chunk 都没有这一条。
scenario_en: A legal RAG answer states a 'clause 7 of the contract' that appears in none of the retrieved chunks.
q: 「答案发明了上下文里没有的合同条款」这类失败，RAG Triad 的哪个维度最直接抓？
q_en: Which RAG Triad dimension most directly catches 'the answer invented a clause not in any chunk'?
why: 答案陈述了检索上下文里根本不存在的内容，就是典型幻觉，直接由 Faithfulness（答案是否忠于上下文）抓住。Relevance 看的是检索是否切题，这里检索可能没问题，问题出在生成脱离了上下文。
why_en: The answer asserts content absent from the retrieved context, which is textbook hallucination caught directly by Faithfulness, since the failure is generation drifting off the context.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题是「检索回来的段落根本不属于这份合同」，那检索本身就跑偏了，该由 Relevance 先抓。
options: Relevance——因为检索到的段落一定和 query 无关
Faithfulness——答案陈述了上下文里不存在的内容
Latency——因为发明条款通常是模型算得太快导致的
Diversity——因为答案缺乏多样化的引用来源
options_en: Relevance — because the retrieved passages must be unrelated to the query.
Faithfulness — the answer states content that is absent from the retrieved context.
Latency — because inventing a clause usually comes from computing too fast.
Diversity — because the answer lacks diverse citation sources.
optionExplanations: 不一定；检索可能完全切题，问题出在生成端脱离了上下文，这不是 Relevance 的失败。
对；发明上下文里没有的内容 = 幻觉，正是 Faithfulness 盯的「答案是否只说上下文支持的话」。
延迟是服务性能，跟答案是否忠于上下文无关，跑得慢也可能编条款。
多样性衡量文字表面，不判断内容是否有上下文支撑，抓不到幻觉。
optionExplanations_en: Not necessarily; retrieval may be perfectly on-topic, with the failure at generation drifting off context — not a Relevance failure.
Correct — inventing content absent from context is hallucination, exactly what Faithfulness watches: does the answer say only what the context supports.
Latency is serving performance, unrelated to faithfulness; a slow system can invent clauses too.
Diversity judges surface text, not whether content is context-supported, so it cannot catch hallucination.

termDefinitions.meaning: 模型生成了检索上下文并不支持的内容，看起来可信但没有依据。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Hallucination is when the model generates content the retrieved context does not support — plausible but unbacked.

tradeoff: Faithfulness（答案↔上下文，抓生成端幻觉）vs Relevance（上下文↔query，抓检索端跑偏）

scenario: 用户问 A 产品线的退货政策，检索器返回的却全是 B 产品线的段落，答案基于这些段落作答。
scenario_en: A user asks about product line A's return policy, but the retriever returns only product line B passages, and the answer is built on them.
q: 「检索回来的 chunk 讨论的是另一条产品线」这类上游失败，该由哪个维度抓？
q_en: Which dimension catches the upstream failure 'retrieved chunks discuss a different product line'?
why: 问题出在检索阶段：拿回来的上下文根本回答不了这个 query，正是 Relevance（上下文↔query 是否切题）盯的上游失败。
why_en: The failure is at retrieval — the context cannot answer the query — which is caught by Relevance, and Faithfulness can even look high while faithfully echoing the wrong passages.
whenOtherWins: 如果检索段落确实是 A 产品线、切题，但答案却编了段落里没有的政策，那问题在生成端，改由 Faithfulness 抓。
options: Groundedness——因为每条主张都缺少段落引用
Fluency——因为答案读起来不通顺
Faithfulness——因为答案一定与上下文矛盾
Relevance——检索上下文与 query 不切题
options_en: Groundedness — because every claim is missing a passage citation.
Fluency — because the answer reads awkwardly.
Faithfulness — because the answer must contradict the context.
Relevance — the retrieved context is off-topic for the query.
optionExplanations: 主张可能都规规矩矩引用了 B 产品线段落，Groundedness 甚至过关，但检索本身错了。
读得通顺与否不解决检索错产品线的问题，答案可能又通顺又错。
忠实复述无关段落时它反而给高分，等于替检索错误打掩护，所以抓不到本题。
对；它只看召回段落与提问是否同一主题，产品线错了就直接扣分，把责任定位到检索器而非模型。
optionExplanations_en: Claims might dutifully cite the product-line-B passages so Groundedness even passes, yet retrieval itself is wrong.
Readability does not fix retrieving the wrong product line; the answer can be fluent and wrong.
It scores high when the model faithfully echoes irrelevant passages, effectively covering for the retrieval error, so it misses this failure.
Correct — it only checks whether the recalled passages share the question topic, so a wrong product line is docked immediately and the blame lands on the retriever, not the model.

termDefinitions.term: upstream retrieval failure / 上游检索失败
termDefinitions.meaning: 检索阶段拿回了无法回答 query 的上下文，问题在生成之前。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An upstream retrieval failure is when retrieval returns context that cannot answer the query, before generation even happens.

tradeoff: Relevance（上下文↔query，抓检索端）vs Faithfulness（答案↔上下文，抓生成端）

scenario: 合规团队要求：AI 给出的每条结论旁边都要能点开看到「出自哪份文件的哪一段」，供审计。
scenario_en: Compliance requires that every AI conclusion can be expanded to show 'which passage of which document it came from,' for audit.
q: 「每条主张都要能指到具体段落做审计」这个需求最匹配哪个维度？
q_en: Which dimension best fits the requirement 'every claim must point to a specific passage for audit'?
why: 审计要的是逐条 attribution——把答案里每一句主张映射到某个 chunk ID、标出无法映射的句子，这正是 Groundedness。Faithfulness 只保证整体不矛盾，给不出「哪句对应哪段」的可审计追踪。
why_en: Audit needs per-claim attribution — mapping each claim to a chunk ID and flagging unmappable ones — which is exactly Groundedness, whereas Faithfulness only guarantees whole-answer consistency.
whenOtherWins: 如果只需要「答案别整体跑偏」、不要求逐句溯源（如内部草稿助手），用更轻的 Faithfulness 就够，省下逐条映射的成本。
options: Relevance——只要检索切题，审计追踪自然就有了
Fluency——审计报告需要答案读起来足够专业
Groundedness——逐条主张映射到段落 ID 的归因报告
Latency——审计要求系统在秒级内响应
options_en: Relevance — as long as retrieval is on-topic, the audit trail comes for free.
Fluency — an audit report needs the answer to read professionally enough.
Groundedness — a per-claim attribution report mapping claims to passage IDs.
Latency — auditing requires the system to respond within seconds.
optionExplanations: 检索切题不代表答案逐句有引用；Relevance 管上游，给不出逐条 attribution。
读起来专业和能否溯源无关，通顺的答案照样可能没有逐条引用。
对；Groundedness 逐条把主张钉到 chunk 上、标出无法归因的句子，正是审计追踪要的东西。
响应快是性能指标，跟每条主张能否溯源到段落完全无关。
optionExplanations_en: On-topic retrieval doesn't mean each sentence is cited; Relevance covers upstream and gives no per-claim attribution.
Reading professionally is unrelated to attributability; a fluent answer can still lack per-claim citations.
Correct — Groundedness pins each claim to a chunk and flags unmappable ones, exactly what an audit trail needs.
Fast response is a performance metric, unrelated to whether each claim traces to a passage.

termDefinitions.meaning: 把答案的每一条主张分别对应到支撑它的段落 ID，无法对应的标记出来。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Per-claim attribution maps each individual claim to the passage ID supporting it, flagging any that cannot be mapped.

tradeoff: Groundedness（逐条主张→段落 ID，可审计）vs Faithfulness（整体不矛盾，成本低）

scenario: 一次评估里，某答案 Faithfulness 打了 5 分（满分），Relevance 却只有 1 分。
scenario_en: In one evaluation an answer scores Faithfulness 5/5 but Relevance only 1/5.
q: 「Faithfulness 高、Relevance 低」这种组合说明系统出了什么问题？
q_en: What does 'high Faithfulness, low Relevance' tell you about the system?
why: 答案很忠实地复述了上下文，但上下文本身跟 query 不搭——即检索拿回了无关内容，模型忠实地在回答「错的问题」。修复要往检索侧走（embedding/召回/重排），而不是改生成 prompt。
why_en: The answer faithfully echoes context that doesn't match the query, meaning retrieval pulled irrelevant content and the model faithfully answered the wrong question, so the fix is on the retrieval side.
options: 检索拿回了无关上下文，模型却忠实复述它——修复应在检索侧（召回/重排），不是改生成
答案有幻觉，模型编造了上下文没有的内容——应加强 Faithfulness 约束
系统延迟过高，需要加缓存
说明两个指标算错了，因为高 Faithfulness 必然伴随高 Relevance
options_en: Retrieval pulled irrelevant context and the model faithfully echoed it — the fix is on the retrieval side (recall/rerank), not generation.
The answer hallucinated content absent from context — tighten Faithfulness constraints.
System latency is too high and needs caching.
The metrics are miscalculated, because high Faithfulness must come with high Relevance.
optionExplanations: 对；高 Faithfulness 说明没编造、忠于上下文，低 Relevance 说明上下文错了，病根在检索。
恰恰相反：Faithfulness 满分说明没幻觉，问题不在生成端而在检索拿错了东西。
延迟和这两个质量维度无关，指标数字不反映速度。
两者独立，高 Faithfulness 完全可以配低 Relevance（忠实地答错问题），并非算错。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — high Faithfulness means no fabrication and fidelity to context, while low Relevance means the context is wrong, so the root cause is retrieval.
Opposite: a perfect Faithfulness score means no hallucination, so the issue is retrieval fetching the wrong thing, not generation.
Latency is unrelated to these two quality dimensions; the scores do not reflect speed.
They are independent — high Faithfulness can pair with low Relevance (faithfully answering the wrong question), so it is not a miscalculation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案忠实复述了检索上下文，但上下文本身与 query 不相关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Faithful-to-irrelevant is when the answer faithfully echoes retrieved context that is itself irrelevant to the query.

scenario: 要在没有海量人工标注的情况下、给每次 pipeline 改动自动打三维分数。
scenario_en: You need to auto-score all three dimensions on each pipeline change without massive human labeling.
q: LLM-as-judge 评估 RAG 的基本做法是什么？
q_en: What is the basic setup of LLM-as-judge for RAG?
why: 用一个独立的 LLM 从结构化输入给每个维度打分，而且每个维度用不同的 prompt——因为三维评估的是不同关系（答案↔上下文、上下文↔query、逐条↔段落），一套通用 prompt 会把它们糊在一起。
why_en: A separate LLM scores each dimension from structured input using a different prompt per dimension, because each dimension evaluates a different relationship that a one-size prompt would blur.
diagram:
flowchart TD I["query + chunks + answer"] --> F["Faithfulness judge
ctx+answer"] I --> R["Relevance judge
只 query+chunks"] I --> G["Groundedness judge
三者+逐条映射"] F --> S["分数 + 问题清单"] R --> S G --> S
options: 让被评的同一个模型给自己的答案打分，省掉单独的评估器
用一个独立 LLM 打分，每个维度用不同 prompt
把三维拼成一个总分让 LLM 一次输出，减少调用次数
只用 BLEU 兜底，LLM 仅在分歧时才介入
options_en: Let the same model being evaluated score its own answers, dropping a separate evaluator.
Use a separate LLM to score, with a different prompt per dimension.
Combine the three dimensions into one total score in a single LLM call to cut calls.
Use BLEU as the fallback and bring in the LLM only on disagreements.
optionExplanations: 自评是既当运动员又当裁判，模型会系统性高估自己，不能当可信评估器。
对；独立 LLM + 每维独立 prompt，才能分别评估三个不同的关系而不互相污染。
三维揉成一个总分会把不同失败糊在一起，恰恰违反「非冗余分开测」的初衷。
BLEU 盲于幻觉和检索错误，兜底也兜不住 RAG 的核心失败模式。
optionExplanations_en: Self-scoring makes the model athlete and referee; it systematically overrates itself and cannot be a trusted evaluator.
Correct — a separate LLM with a per-dimension prompt evaluates the three distinct relationships without cross-contamination.
Merging three into one total score blends distinct failures, violating the whole point of non-redundant separate measurement.
BLEU is blind to hallucination and retrieval errors, so it cannot backstop RAG's core failure modes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用一个独立 LLM 对另一个系统的输出按给定标准打分，替代部分人工评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM-as-judge uses a separate LLM to score another system's output against given criteria, replacing some human evaluation.

termDefinitions.meaning: 大语言模型，这里指用来打分的评审模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LLM (Large Language Model) here refers to the model used to score outputs.

scenario: 设计 Relevance 判官的输入时，要决定「要不要把生成的答案也喂给它」。
scenario_en: Designing the Relevance judge's input, you must decide whether to also feed it the generated answer.
q: Relevance 判官为什么只喂 query + chunks，故意不给它答案？
q_en: Why is the Relevance judge given only query + chunks, deliberately excluding the answer?
why: Relevance 只评「检索上下文是否切题」，跟答案无关。把一个流畅但不忠实的答案喂进去，会诱导判官被文笔带偏、误判上下文相关性，所以刻意排除答案。Faithfulness/Groundedness 判官才需要答案。
why_en: Relevance only judges whether the retrieved context fits the query, so feeding in a fluent-but-unfaithful answer would sway the judge by surface fluency and bias the relevance verdict.
whenOtherWins: 评 Faithfulness 或 Groundedness 时必须给答案——因为那两维恰恰要比对「答案 vs 上下文」，缺了答案没法判。
options: 因为把答案也传进去会超出判官的上下文窗口，纯属省 token
因为答案属于隐私数据，判官按合规要求不允许看到
因为 Relevance 只评上下文↔query，答案会带偏判官
因为答案总是正确的，给不给判官都不影响相关性判断
options_en: Because passing the answer in too would overflow the judge's context window — purely token saving.
Because the answer is private data the judge is not allowed to see under compliance rules.
Because Relevance only judges context-versus-query, and the answer would sway the judge.
Because the answer is always correct, so including it doesn't change the relevance verdict.
optionExplanations: 省 token 不是主因，chunks 通常比答案长得多；核心是防止答案污染相关性判断。
隐私不是这里的理由，判官本来就在处理这些数据；关键是评估维度的纯净性。
对；相关性只该看上下文与 query 的匹配，一段文笔好的错答案会诱导判官高估相关性。
答案常常不正确（幻觉/无关），且相关性根本不该由答案来定，这个前提就是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Token saving is not the driver — chunks are usually far longer than the answer; the core reason is preventing the answer from polluting the relevance verdict.
Privacy is not the reason; the judge already handles this data — the point is keeping the evaluation dimension clean.
Correct — relevance should only weigh context against the query, and a well-written wrong answer would nudge the judge to overrate relevance.
Answers are often wrong (hallucinated/irrelevant), and relevance should never be set by the answer, so this premise is false.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判官被答案的流畅表达误导，把文笔好当成质量高。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Fluency sway is when the judge is misled by a fluent answer, mistaking good prose for high quality.

scenario: 设计 Faithfulness 判官：要判「答案里每句话是否都被检索上下文支持」。
scenario_en: Designing the Faithfulness judge: decide whether every sentence in the answer is supported by the retrieved context.
q: Faithfulness 判官的输入和输出应该是什么？
q_en: What should the Faithfulness judge's input and output be?
why: 输入 = 上下文 + 答案（要比对二者）；输出 = 一个分数 + 一份「未被支持主张」清单。清单让评估不止给分，还能定位到底哪句在幻觉，方便回炉修生成 prompt。
why_en: Input is context plus answer to compare them, and output is a score plus a list of unsupported claims so you know which sentences hallucinated, not just an opaque number.
options: 输入上下文+答案，输出一个分数 + 未被支持主张的清单
输入只有 query，输出一个 1-100 的绝对分
输入 query+答案（不给上下文），输出通过/不通过
输入上下文，输出重写后的正确答案
options_en: Input context plus answer, output a score plus a list of unsupported claims.
Input only the query, output an absolute 1-100 score.
Input query plus answer (no context), output pass/fail.
Input the context, output a rewritten correct answer.
optionExplanations: 对；要判忠实必须同时看上下文和答案，输出配一份未支持主张清单才能定位幻觉句。
只给 query 无从比对上下文，绝对分也噪声大，判不了忠实性。
不给上下文就无法判断答案是否被上下文支持，缺了比对对象。
判官的活是打分和定位问题，不是重写答案；重写是生成器的职责。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — judging faithfulness needs both context and answer, and an unsupported-claims list locates the hallucinated sentences.
The query alone gives nothing to compare against the context, and absolute scores are noisy, so faithfulness can't be judged.
Without context you cannot judge whether the answer is context-supported — the comparison target is missing.
The judge's job is scoring and locating issues, not rewriting the answer; rewriting is the generator's job.

termDefinitions.meaning: 答案里一条无法在检索上下文中找到依据的陈述。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An unsupported claim is a statement in the answer with no backing found in the retrieved context.

scenario: 设计 Groundedness 判官，要产出可审计的逐条溯源报告。
scenario_en: Designing the Groundedness judge to produce an auditable per-claim attribution report.
q: Groundedness 判官的输入和工作方式是什么？
q_en: What is the Groundedness judge's input and how does it work?
why: 输入三样全给：query + chunks + 答案；然后把答案里每条主张映射到某个 chunk ID，标出无法映射的主张，产出逐条 attribution 报告。它比 Faithfulness 判官多做「逐条对齐到具体段落」这一步。
why_en: It takes all three inputs — query, chunks, answer — then maps each claim to a chunk ID and flags unmappable claims, producing a per-claim attribution report.
options: 只输入答案，靠模型常识判断哪些主张听起来可信，不看检索内容
只输入 chunks，输出每个 chunk 对 query 的相关性排名
输入 query+chunks+答案，逐条主张映射到 chunk ID
输入 query+答案，输出整体是否可信的布尔值，不做逐条对齐
options_en: Input only the answer and use the model's common sense to judge which claims sound credible, ignoring retrieval.
Input only the chunks and output each chunk's relevance ranking for the query.
Input query+chunks+answer and map each claim to a chunk ID.
Input query+answer and output one boolean for overall credibility, with no per-claim alignment.
optionExplanations: 常识判可信违背了「可溯源」的初衷，Groundedness 要的是指到具体段落，不是听起来对。
只给 chunks 排相关性是 Relevance 的活，不是逐条归因。
对；三样输入齐全才能逐条把主张钉到 chunk 上，无法归因的标出来，形成审计追踪。
布尔值太粗，给不出「哪句对应哪段」的逐条报告，达不到审计粒度。
optionExplanations_en: Judging credibility by common sense defeats attributability; Groundedness needs pointers to specific passages, not 'sounds right.'
Ranking chunks by relevance is Relevance's job, not per-claim attribution.
Correct — all three inputs let it pin each claim to a chunk and flag unmappable ones, forming an audit trail.
A boolean is too coarse to give the per-claim 'which sentence maps to which passage' report needed for audit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 文档被切成的可检索小片段，检索和引用都以 chunk 为单位。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A chunk is a small retrievable slice a document is split into; retrieval and citation operate per chunk.

scenario: LLM 判官直接输出一个分数时，常常被答案的流畅度带偏，打分不稳定。
scenario_en: When the LLM judge outputs a score directly, it is often swayed by fluency and scores inconsistently.
q: 为什么让 LLM 判官用 chain-of-thought（先推理再打分）能提升可靠性？
q_en: Why does chain-of-thought (reason first, then score) improve the LLM judge's reliability?
why: 强制判官先一步步列出「哪条主张、被哪段支持/不支持」，再给分，就不会只凭表面文笔拍脑袋。省掉推理步骤时，判官容易被流畅度诱导，给通顺但错误的答案打高分。代价是多花 token 和延迟。
why_en: Forcing step-by-step reasoning before scoring stops the judge from grading on surface fluency, at the cost of more tokens and latency.
tradeoff: CoT（推理更稳但更贵/更慢）vs 直接打分（快但易被文笔带偏）
options: 因为 CoT 让模型输出更长，长答案天然更准确
因为强制先逐步核对每条主张再打分，避免只凭表面文笔拍脑袋
因为 CoT 能减少 token 消耗，降低评估成本
因为 CoT 让判官跳过检索上下文，直接凭常识评分更快
options_en: Because CoT makes the output longer, and longer outputs are inherently more accurate.
Because forcing step-by-step checking of each claim before scoring avoids grading on surface fluency.
Because CoT reduces token consumption and lowers evaluation cost.
Because CoT lets the judge skip the context and score faster from common sense.
optionExplanations: 长≠准，长输出本身不带来准确性；起作用的是「先推理核对」这个过程，不是长度。
对；一步步核对主张与依据，判官就得看证据而非文笔，打分更稳定可复现。
CoT 其实增加 token 和延迟，是它的代价，不是省钱的手段。
跳过上下文恰恰会让评分失去依据，与提升可靠性背道而驰。
optionExplanations_en: Longer isn't more accurate; length alone helps nothing — the 'reason and verify first' process does, not length.
Correct — checking each claim against evidence step by step forces the judge to look at evidence not prose, giving stabler reproducible scores.
CoT actually adds tokens and latency — that is its cost, not a way to save money.
Skipping the context removes the grounding for scoring, the opposite of improving reliability.

termDefinitions.meaning: 让模型在给结论前先逐步写出推理过程，提升判断可靠性。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting has the model write out step-by-step reasoning before its conclusion, improving reliability.

scenario: 用 LLM 当裁判打分前，要先知道它系统性偏差在哪，否则分数不可信。
scenario_en: Before trusting an LLM judge's scores, you must know its systematic biases or the scores are untrustworthy.
q: LLM 判官有哪些已知的系统性偏差？(多选)
q_en: Which systematic biases do LLM judges have? (multiple)
why: 三种典型偏差：position bias（偏向排在前面的选项）、verbosity bias（偏向更长的答案）、self-enhancement bias（偏向和自己同一模型家族的输出）。它们都会系统性扭曲分数，必须专门缓解。
why_en: The three known biases are position bias (favors the first option), verbosity bias (prefers longer answers), and self-enhancement bias (favors its own model family).
options: Position bias：偏向排在前面的选项
Verbosity bias：偏向更长的答案
Self-enhancement bias：偏向和自己同家族模型的输出
Thermal bias：GPU 温度升高时打分变严
options_en: Position bias: favors the option shown first.
Verbosity bias: prefers longer answers.
Self-enhancement bias: favors output from its own model family.
Thermal bias: scores stricter as GPU temperature rises.
optionExplanations: 对；同样两个选项，仅调换顺序判官就可能改判，所以要随机化顺序。
对；判官容易把「更长/更详细」误当成「更好」，需用人工标签校准。
对；判官偏爱和自己同一模型家族的风格，用多家族判官投票可缓解。
错；GPU 温度是硬件指标，不影响模型的打分逻辑，这是编造的偏差。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — swapping only the order of two options can flip the verdict, so randomize order.
Correct — the judge tends to mistake 'longer/more detailed' for 'better,' needing calibration against human labels.
Correct — the judge prefers its own model family's style, mitigated by multi-family judge voting.
Wrong — GPU temperature is a hardware metric and does not affect scoring logic; this bias is fabricated.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判官系统性偏向呈现在前面的候选，与内容无关。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Position bias is the judge systematically favoring whichever candidate is presented first, regardless of content.

termDefinitions.meaning: 判官把更长、更啰嗦的答案误判为更好。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Verbosity bias is the judge mistaking longer, wordier answers for better ones.

termDefinitions.term: self-enhancement bias / 自我强化偏差
termDefinitions.meaning: 判官偏爱与自己同一模型家族生成的输出。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Self-enhancement bias is the judge favoring outputs generated by its own model family.

scenario: 让 LLM 判官在 A、B 两个答案里选更好的一个，你发现它总倾向选先出现的那个。
scenario_en: Asking an LLM judge to pick the better of answers A and B, you find it keeps favoring whichever appears first.
q: 针对 position bias（偏向第一个选项），最直接的缓解手段是什么？
q_en: What most directly mitigates position bias (favoring the first option)?
why: 随机化选项呈现顺序，或对调顺序各判一次再取一致结果，就能把「先后位置」这个和内容无关的因素平均掉。多模型或校准解决的是别的偏差，对纯位置效应不对症。
why_en: Randomize the option order (or judge both orderings and require agreement) to average out the content-irrelevant position factor.
whenOtherWins: 如果问题不是位置而是判官偏爱自家风格，那随机顺序没用，得换成多家族判官。
options: 随机化选项呈现顺序，或对调顺序各判一次取一致
只用同一家族的多个判官投票，统一风格
要求答案尽量简短，减少 token
把两个答案拼成一段，让判官打一个总分
options_en: Randomize option order, or judge both orderings and require agreement.
Use multiple judges from the same family to vote, unifying style.
Require answers to be as short as possible to reduce tokens.
Concatenate both answers into one passage and have the judge give a single score.
optionExplanations: 对；位置偏差只跟呈现顺序有关，打乱顺序或双向各判一次就能把它平均消掉。
同家族投票会放大 self-enhancement，且不解决位置效应，方向错了。
缩短答案是对 verbosity bias 的间接想法，跟「偏向第一个」无关。
拼成一段反而丢了 A/B 的边界，无法比较，也没消除位置影响。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — position bias depends only on ordering, so shuffling or judging both directions averages it out.
Same-family voting amplifies self-enhancement and doesn't touch position — wrong direction.
Shortening answers targets verbosity bias indirectly and is unrelated to favoring the first option.
Concatenating loses the A/B boundary, preventing comparison and not removing position effects.

termDefinitions.term: randomize option order / 随机化选项顺序
termDefinitions.meaning: 把候选答案的呈现顺序打乱或双向各判一次，消除位置偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Randomizing option order shuffles candidate ordering (or judges both directions) to cancel position bias.

tradeoff: 随机化顺序（治位置偏差，几乎零成本）vs 多家族判官/人工校准（治别的偏差，更贵）

scenario: 你的答案生成器和 LLM 判官用的是同一家公司同一系列的模型，怀疑判官在偏袒自家风格。
scenario_en: Your generator and your LLM judge are the same company's model series, and you suspect the judge favors its own style.
q: 针对 self-enhancement bias（偏袒同家族模型），最对症的缓解是什么？
q_en: What most directly mitigates self-enhancement bias (favoring its own model family)?
why: 用来自不同模型家族的多个判官分别打分再综合，抵消任何单一家族的自我偏袒。随机顺序治位置偏差、人工校准治冗长偏差，都不对症自我强化这条。
why_en: Use multiple judges from different model families and combine their scores to cancel any single family's self-favoritism.
whenOtherWins: 如果偏差来自「总选第一个」，那多家族判官帮不上，应改用随机化选项顺序。
options: 把答案改短，减少判官被内容量影响
固定选项顺序，保证每次评估条件一致
用不同模型家族的多个判官打分再综合
只保留一个最强的判官，减少噪声来源
options_en: Shorten the answers to reduce how content volume affects the judge.
Fix the option order to keep every evaluation under identical conditions.
Use multiple judges from different model families and combine their scores.
Keep only one strongest judge to reduce noise sources.
optionExplanations: 改短针对的是 verbosity，不解决判官偏袒自家家族的问题。
固定顺序反而会固化 position bias，也管不了自我强化。
对；不同家族互不偏袒彼此，多家族综合能把任一家族的自我偏好平均掉。
只留一个判官恰恰无法消除它自己的家族偏好，反而更危险。
optionExplanations_en: Shortening targets verbosity, not the judge favoring its own family.
Fixing order actually entrenches position bias and does nothing for self-enhancement.
Correct — different families don't favor each other, so combining across families averages out any one family's self-preference.
Keeping a single judge cannot remove that judge's own family preference — it makes it worse.

termDefinitions.meaning: 用来自不同模型家族的多个 LLM 分别评分再综合，降低单一模型偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A multi-model judge uses several LLMs from different families to score and combine, reducing any single model's bias.

tradeoff: 多家族判官（治自我偏袒，评估成本翻倍）vs 单判官（便宜但带家族偏好）

scenario: 判官似乎把更长、更啰嗦的答案打得更高，即便短答案其实更准。
scenario_en: The judge seems to score longer, wordier answers higher even when a short answer is actually more accurate.
q: 针对 verbosity bias（偏爱长答案），最对症的缓解是什么？
q_en: What most directly mitigates verbosity bias (preferring longer answers)?
why: 拿人工标签当锚校准判官——用人已知的好坏样本去检查判官是否把「长」错当「好」，据此调 prompt 或做后处理修正。随机顺序治位置、多家族治自我强化，都不针对长度偏好。
why_en: Calibrate the judge against human labels to detect and correct where it mistakes 'longer' for 'better,' then tune the prompt accordingly.
whenOtherWins: 如果偏差其实来自选项顺序或同家族偏袒，校准长度就不对症，应分别用随机顺序或多家族判官。
options: 把所有答案截断成同样长度，强行去掉长度差异
让判官对更长的答案自动加分，顺应它的偏好
只用单一判官，减少不同长度带来的分歧
用人工标签校准判官，检查并纠正它把「长」当「好」
options_en: Truncate all answers to the same length to force away length differences.
Have the judge auto-bonus longer answers, going along with its preference.
Use a single judge to reduce disagreement from differing lengths.
Calibrate the judge against human labels to detect and correct 'longer means better.'
optionExplanations: 强行截断会破坏答案完整性、误伤该长的答案，是粗暴的错解。
顺应偏好等于放大 verbosity bias，方向完全反了。
单判官既不校准也不揭示长度偏好，问题依旧。
对；用人已知好坏的样本当锚，就能量出判官的长度偏好并回调 prompt 或分数。
optionExplanations_en: Forced truncation breaks answer completeness and penalizes rightfully long answers — a crude wrong fix.
Going along with the preference amplifies verbosity bias — exactly backwards.
A single judge neither calibrates nor reveals the length preference; the problem persists.
Correct — human-labeled good/bad samples anchor the judge, exposing its length bias so you can retune the prompt or scores.

termDefinitions.term: calibrate vs human labels / 对人工标签校准
termDefinitions.meaning: 用人已知正误的样本对照判官打分，量出并纠正它的系统偏差。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Calibrating against human labels compares judge scores to known-correct samples to measure and correct systematic bias.

tradeoff: 人工标签校准（治冗长偏差，准但费人力）vs 纯自动判官（便宜但偏好长答案）

scenario: 三维评估每个样本要跑 3 次判官调用，直接对全部线上流量评估会烧掉大量 LLM 成本。
scenario_en: Three-dimension evaluation costs 3 judge calls per example, and running it on all live traffic burns huge LLM cost.
q: 三维 LLM 判官成本高（每样本 3 次调用），评估策略该怎么设计？
q_en: Given the high cost (3 judge calls per example), how should the evaluation strategy be designed?
why: 别对全量流量评估，而是在一个统计上有代表性的样本上做批量评估——让评估成本正比于「pipeline 改动频率」而非「流量大小」。每改一次 pipeline 跑一批就够，流量翻十倍不必评估也翻十倍。
why_en: Batch-evaluate a statistically representative sample so cost scales with how often the pipeline changes, not with traffic volume.
tradeoff: 代表性抽样批量评估（省钱、够用）vs 全量评估（昂贵、多为冗余重复）
options: 对每一条线上请求都实时跑三维评估，保证无遗漏
在有代表性的样本上批量评估，成本随改动频率而非流量
砍到只评一个维度，牺牲另外两维换成本
把判官换成 BLEU 以省钱，反正差别不大
options_en: Run three-dimension evaluation in real time on every live request to miss nothing.
Batch-evaluate a representative sample so cost scales with change frequency, not traffic.
Cut to only one dimension, trading the other two for cost.
Replace judges with BLEU to save money, since the difference is small.
optionExplanations: 全量实时评估把成本绑在流量上，代价高且大量重复，没必要。
对；一个代表性样本足以反映系统质量，成本随改动频率走，才是可持续的评估经济学。
砍维度会漏掉一整类失败（如漏 Relevance 就看不见检索错），是拿准确性换钱。
BLEU 盲于幻觉和检索错误，省下的钱换来看不见核心失败，得不偿失。
optionExplanations_en: Full real-time evaluation ties cost to traffic — expensive and largely redundant, unnecessary.
Correct — a representative sample reflects system quality, and cost tracking change frequency is sustainable evaluation economics.
Cutting a dimension drops a whole failure class (drop Relevance and you miss retrieval errors) — trading accuracy for money.
BLEU is blind to hallucination and retrieval errors, so the savings buy invisibility to core failures — a bad trade.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按查询类型/难度分布抽取的一小批数据，能反映整体质量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A representative sample is a small batch drawn across query types and difficulty that reflects overall quality.

scenario: 要用人工评估给自动打分做校准，设计标注任务时决定标注者该怎么打分。
scenario_en: Setting up human evaluation to calibrate automated scores, you decide how annotators should rate.
q: 人工评估 RAG 时，标注任务应该怎么组织打分？
q_en: How should the human RAG evaluation task be organized for scoring?
why: 给标注者看 query + chunks + 答案，让 ta 对每个维度独立打分，而不是给一个笼统的「总体好不好」。独立打分才能定位是忠实性、相关性还是溯源性出问题，也才能和三维自动分对齐校准。
why_en: Show the annotator query + chunks + answer and have them rate each dimension independently, not one holistic score, so failures can be localized.
options: 只给答案，让标注者凭整体印象打一个笼统的总分
让标注者写出理想答案，用与之的编辑距离当分数
给 query+chunks+答案，对每个维度独立打分
让标注者只判「通过/不通过」一个布尔值，不分维度
options_en: Show only the answer and have the annotator give one holistic impression score.
Have annotators write the ideal answer and use edit distance to it as the score.
Show query+chunks+answer and rate each dimension independently.
Have annotators give only a pass/fail boolean, with no per-dimension split.
optionExplanations: 只看答案没有上下文对照，也无法分维度，笼统总分定位不了问题。
写理想答案+编辑距离又退回到字面重叠，测不出忠实/相关/溯源。
对；三样齐看、逐维独立打分，才能分辨是哪一维失败，并与自动分对齐校准。
布尔值太粗，既不分维度也给不了 1-5 的梯度，无法做细致校准。
optionExplanations_en: The answer alone lacks context and no dimensions, so a holistic score cannot localize the problem.
Writing an ideal answer plus edit distance regresses to surface overlap, missing faithfulness/relevance/attribution.
Correct — seeing all three and rating each dimension independently distinguishes which dimension failed and aligns with automated scores.
A boolean is too coarse, with no dimensions and no 1-5 gradient for fine calibration.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对答案只给一个整体好坏分，不拆维度，难以定位具体失败。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A holistic score gives one overall good/bad rating without breaking into dimensions, making failures hard to localize.

scenario: 两个标注者对同一个答案的 Faithfulness 一个打 4、一个打 2，因为「好/差」全凭各自理解。
scenario_en: Two annotators score the same answer's Faithfulness 4 and 2 because 'good/bad' is left to personal interpretation.
q: 为什么 1–5 Likert 量表每个分数都要写明确的锚点描述？
q_en: Why must each point of a 1-5 Likert scale have an explicit anchor description?
why: 给每个分值写清判据（如 Faithfulness：1=与上下文矛盾，5=每条主张都被支持），标注者才有统一尺子，一致性才高。只写「好/差」没有锚点，人各有各的标准，标签方差大、不可信。
why_en: Explicit per-point anchors (e.g. 1 = contradicts context, 5 = every claim supported) give annotators one shared ruler, raising agreement, whereas vague 'good/bad' produces high-variance labels.
whenOtherWins: 如果任务本就有客观对错（如答案是否精确匹配某个数字），可以用二元判据，不必细化 1-5 锚点。
options: 写明每个分值的判据（1=与上下文矛盾，5=全部支持）
锚点主要为了让评分表看起来专业，对一致性无实质影响
锚点是为了让标注者打分更快，与准确性无关
锚点能替代 IAA 测量，有了锚点就不用算一致性了
options_en: Spell out the criteria per point (1 = contradicts context, 5 = fully supported).
Anchors mainly make the rubric look professional, with no real effect on agreement.
Anchors just make annotators score faster, unrelated to accuracy.
Anchors can replace IAA measurement, so with anchors you skip computing agreement.
optionExplanations: 对；每分值有可判定的描述，两个标注者才会在同一把尺子上打分，方差自然降下来。
锚点不是装饰，它直接决定一致性——没有它同一答案可能被打 2 也可能被打 4。
锚点主要提升一致性和准确性，不是单纯提速。
锚点提升一致性，但仍要用 IAA 量化验证，两者互补不能互相替代。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — a decidable description per point puts two annotators on the same ruler, cutting variance.
Anchors are not decoration; they directly drive agreement — without them the same answer gets a 2 or a 4.
Anchors mainly raise consistency and accuracy, not merely speed.
Anchors raise agreement but you still quantify with IAA; they complement rather than replace it.

termDefinitions.meaning: 如 1-5 的有序评分量表，每级最好配明确的锚点描述。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A Likert scale is an ordered rating (e.g. 1-5), ideally with an explicit anchor description per level.

termDefinitions.meaning: 对量表每个分值给出的可判定标准，统一标注者的尺度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An anchor description is a decidable criterion for each scale point, unifying annotators' scale.

tradeoff: 锚点化 rubric（写起来慢，但 IAA 高、标签可信）vs 笼统好/差量表（快但方差大）

scenario: 校准数据集上算出标注者间一致性（IAA）的 Cohen's kappa 只有 0.45。
scenario_en: On the calibration set, inter-annotator agreement (IAA) Cohen's kappa comes out at only 0.45.
q: IAA 低于 0.6 说明什么，该先做什么？
q_en: What does IAA below 0.6 indicate, and what should you do first?
why: IAA<0.6 通常说明 rubric 本身有歧义、标注者理解不一，此时标签不可信，别急着拿去校准判官。应先修订 rubric（细化锚点、澄清边界），一致性达标后标签才有意义。
why_en: IAA below 0.6 usually means the rubric is ambiguous, so the labels are untrustworthy and you should revise the rubric before trusting or using them.
tradeoff: 先修 rubric 提一致性（慢但标签可信）vs 直接用低一致性标签（快但污染校准基准）
options: 说明标注者不够努力，换一批更认真的人重标即可
说明 rubric 有歧义、标签不可信，应先修订它
说明模型答案质量太差，应该先去改生成模型
0.45 已经够高，可以直接拿这批标签校准判官
options_en: It means annotators aren't trying hard; just swap in more diligent people and relabel.
It means the rubric is ambiguous and the labels untrustworthy — revise it first.
It means the model answers are too poor and you should fix the generator first.
0.45 is already high enough to calibrate the judge with these labels directly.
optionExplanations: 换人治标不治本，歧义在 rubric 上，不细化锚点换谁都对不齐。
对；低一致性首先怪 rubric 不清，先把判据改明确，标签才配当校准基准。
IAA 量的是标注者之间是否一致，跟模型答案好坏无关，方向错了。
0.45 明显低于 0.6 的经验阈值，用它校准等于拿噪声当真值。
optionExplanations_en: Swapping people treats the symptom; the ambiguity is in the rubric, and without sharper anchors no one aligns.
Correct — low agreement first indicts an unclear rubric; sharpen the criteria before the labels can serve as a calibration baseline.
IAA measures whether annotators agree, unrelated to model answer quality — wrong direction.
0.45 is well below the 0.6 rule-of-thumb threshold; calibrating with it means treating noise as ground truth.

termDefinitions.meaning: 标注者间一致性：不同标注者对同一样本给出相同评分的程度。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: IAA (Inter-Annotator Agreement) measures how often different annotators give the same rating to the same item.

termDefinitions.meaning: 两名标注者一致性的统计量，扣除了随机一致的成分。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cohen's kappa is a statistic for two annotators' agreement, correcting for chance agreement.

scenario: 要量化 RAG 标注的一致性，团队规模从 2 人到十几人不等，得选对统计量。
scenario_en: To quantify RAG labeling agreement with teams ranging from 2 to a dozen annotators, you must pick the right statistic.
q: 衡量 IAA 时，Cohen's kappa 和 Krippendorff's alpha 各用在什么场景？
q_en: For IAA, when do you use Cohen's kappa versus Krippendorff's alpha?
why: Cohen's kappa 适合恰好两名标注者的一致性；标注团队更大（多标注者、可能有缺失评分）时用 Krippendorff's alpha，它天然支持任意标注者数和缺失数据。两者都扣除了随机一致成分。
why_en: Cohen's kappa fits exactly two annotators, while Krippendorff's alpha handles larger teams and missing ratings, both correcting for chance agreement.
tradeoff: Cohen's kappa（两人、简单）vs Krippendorff's alpha（多人/有缺失、通用）
options: 两者可互换，标注者多少都不影响，随便用哪个都一样
Cohen's kappa 用于恰好 2 名标注者；Krippendorff's alpha 用于更大团队或缺失数据
Cohen's kappa 用于大团队多标注者，Krippendorff's alpha 只能用于恰好 2 人
Cohen's kappa 测标注准确率，Krippendorff's alpha 测标注召回率
options_en: They are interchangeable; the number of annotators doesn't matter, use either.
Cohen's kappa is for exactly 2 annotators; Krippendorff's alpha for larger teams or missing data.
Cohen's kappa is for large multi-annotator teams and Krippendorff's alpha only for exactly 2 people.
Cohen's kappa measures annotation accuracy and Krippendorff's alpha measures annotation recall.
optionExplanations: 两者适用的标注者规模不同，不能随便互换。
对；kappa 天生只处理两人，alpha 支持任意人数和缺失评分，按团队规模选。
说反了：kappa 才是两人的，alpha 才支持大团队。
两者都是一致性统计量，不是准确率/召回率，这个对应是错的。
optionExplanations_en: They apply to different annotator counts and are not freely interchangeable.
Correct — kappa handles two annotators, alpha any count plus missing ratings, so choose by team size.
Backwards: kappa is the two-annotator one and alpha handles large teams.
Both are agreement statistics, not accuracy/recall — this mapping is wrong.

termDefinitions.meaning: 适用于任意标注者数、可处理缺失数据的一致性统计量。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Krippendorff's alpha is an agreement statistic for any number of annotators that also handles missing data.

scenario: 要给三维自动评估建一个可信的人工校准基准，决定标多少、怎么抽。
scenario_en: Building a trustworthy human calibration baseline for the three-dimension automated eval, you decide how many to label and how to sample.
q: 填空：RAG 人工校准的起点规模与抽样方式。
q_en: Fill in the blanks: starting size and sampling for human RAG calibration.
text: 校准起点：每个维度约 {{200–300}} 条人工标注，并按查询类型/难度做 {{分层(stratified)}} 抽样以避免采样偏差。这是经验起点、不是公式推导；它是校准判官、监控判官漂移的基数。
text_en: Calibration starting point: about {{200–300}} human annotations per dimension, {{stratified}} across query types/difficulty to avoid sampling bias — an empirical starting point, not a formula, and the base for calibrating the judge and monitoring drift.
why: 200–300/维度是常见经验起点（不是算出来的），少了统计不稳、多了成本浪费；分层抽样保证简单/困难/各类查询都覆盖，避免基准只反映某一类查询。这批标注是校准判官、监控判官漂移的锚。
why_en: About 200–300 per dimension is an empirical starting point, and stratified sampling ensures easy/hard and varied query types are covered so the baseline isn't skewed to one query class.

termDefinitions.meaning: 按查询类型、难度等分层各抽一部分，保证样本覆盖不同子群。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Stratified sampling draws from each stratum (query type, difficulty) so the sample covers different subgroups.

codeSample:
# 每维 250 条：经验起点，不是公式推导出来的数字
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
cal, _ = train_test_split(
    logs, train_size=250,
    stratify=logs["query_type"],   # 分层键：简单/多跳/长尾各按比例抽
    random_state=42)               # 固定种子，判官漂移复测时可复现同一批
cal.to_json("golden_faithfulness.jsonl", orient="records", lines=True)

scenario: 上线后要持续监控 RAG 质量，团队讨论离线评估和在线评估各自负责什么。
scenario_en: After launch you must continuously monitor RAG quality; the team debates what offline versus online evaluation each handles.
q: 生产环境里 offline 评估和 online 评估各自的角色是什么？
q_en: In production, what are the roles of offline versus online evaluation?
why: Offline：每次 pipeline 改动后在留出集上跑判官做回归，金标集监控漂移。Online：抽样真实流量人工复核，反哺 prompt 调优。
why_en: Offline runs LLM-judge regression on a held-out set after every pipeline change with golden sets monitoring judge drift, while online samples live traffic for async human review that feeds back into judge-prompt tuning.
tradeoff: Offline（受控回归、每次改动都跑）vs Online（真实流量抽样、异步人工复核）

rows: 人工复核、反哺 prompt 调优

options: Offline 在留出集上跑回归并测判官漂移；Online 抽样真实流量人工复核
Offline 只在上线前跑一次，之后全靠 Online 监控，无需再做任何回归
Offline 用真实流量、Online 用留出集，二者数据来源刚好相反，用途也相反
两者都只用自动判官，不涉及任何人工，区别只是跑的时间点
options_en: Offline runs regression and drift checks on a held-out set; Online samples live traffic for human review.
Offline runs once before launch, then everything relies on Online monitoring with no more regression.
Offline uses live traffic and Online uses a held-out set — the data sources and purposes are exactly reversed.
Both use only automated judges with no humans; the only difference is when they run.
optionExplanations: 对；离线是受控回归（每改必跑、金标测漂移），在线是真实流量抽检+人工复核，闭合校准环。
只上线前跑一次就不管了，检测不到之后改动引入的回归，站不住。
数据来源说反了：离线才用留出集，在线才抽真实流量。
在线恰恰要引入人工复核来校准判官，说「全无人工」是错的。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — offline is controlled regression (run on every change, golden sets catch drift), online is live sampling plus human review, closing the loop.
Running once pre-launch misses regressions introduced by later changes — untenable.
Data sources reversed: offline uses the held-out set, online samples live traffic.
Online specifically brings in human review to calibrate the judge, so 'no humans' is wrong.

termDefinitions.term: held-out test set / 留出测试集
termDefinitions.meaning: 固定的、不参与训练的评估集，用来做可复现的回归测试。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A held-out test set is a fixed, non-training evaluation set used for reproducible regression testing.

scenario: 你的 LLM 判官用了几个月，怀疑它的打分口径慢慢变了，但没有对照就发现不了。
scenario_en: Your LLM judge has run for months and you suspect its scoring has slowly shifted, but with no reference you can't tell.
q: 人工标注的「金标集（golden set）」在生产评估里起什么作用？
q_en: What role does a human-annotated golden set play in production evaluation?
why: 把判官定期在一个稳定的人工金标集上重跑，分数若相对历史基线漂了，就说明判官口径变了（模型升级、prompt 改动引起）。金标集是不动的标尺，用来监控 judge drift，否则自动分悄悄跑偏也无人察觉。
why_en: Re-running the judge on a stable golden set against a historical baseline reveals judge drift, since the golden set is the fixed ruler that would otherwise be missing.
options: 金标集是拿来训练生成模型的高质量语料
作为稳定标尺定期重测判官，分数偏离基线即暴露漂移
金标集用来替代所有自动评估，之后不再需要判官
金标集只在上线第一天用一次，之后作废
options_en: The golden set is high-quality corpus for training the generator.
As a stable ruler re-tested periodically; drift from the baseline exposes judge drift.
The golden set replaces all automated evaluation so judges are no longer needed.
The golden set is used only on launch day, then discarded.
optionExplanations: 金标集是评估基准，不是训练语料，用途搞混了。
对；固定的人工标签当不动标尺，判官再跑分若偏离基线，就抓到了它的漂移。
金标集是监控判官的锚，不能取代自动判官（自动判官负责规模化打分）。
只用一天就废，就失去了持续监控漂移的意义，得反复重测。
optionExplanations_en: The golden set is an evaluation baseline, not training corpus — uses confused.
Correct — fixed human labels are the unmoving ruler; if the judge's re-scoring diverges from baseline, you've caught its drift.
The golden set anchors monitoring of the judge; it cannot replace the automated judge that does scale scoring.
Using it once and discarding loses continuous drift monitoring; it must be re-tested repeatedly.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一批稳定的、人工确认过的评估样本，用作监控判官漂移的固定基线。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A golden set is a stable, human-verified evaluation set used as a fixed baseline to monitor judge drift.

termDefinitions.meaning: 自动判官的打分口径随模型或 prompt 变化而悄悄偏移。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Judge drift is when the automated judge's scoring criteria silently shift as the model or prompt changes.

scenario: 自动评估便宜、能持续跑，但会漂；人工评估准，但贵又慢。要设计长期评估机制。
scenario_en: Automated evaluation is cheap and continuous but drifts; human evaluation is accurate but slow and costly. Design a long-term scheme.
q: 面对「自动可扩展但会漂 / 人工准但贵」的核心权衡，评估机制该怎么组合？
q_en: Given 'automated scales but drifts / human is accurate but costly,' how should the scheme combine them?
why: 用自动评估做持续回归测试（每次改动都跑、便宜可扩展），再周期性安排人工标注冲刺来校准判官、纠正漂移。两者互补：自动扛规模，人工守准确，谁也替代不了谁。
why_en: Use automated evaluation for continuous regression testing and periodic human annotation sprints to calibrate the judge and correct drift, letting each cover the other's weakness.
tradeoff: 自动（可扩展但漂）+ 人工（准但贵）→ 自动做回归、人工做周期校准
options: 全自动，彻底放弃人工，接受漂移
全人工，彻底放弃自动，接受慢和贵
自动和人工随机各占一半，不区分职责
自动做持续回归，人工周期性冲刺校准判官
options_en: Fully automated, drop humans entirely, accept the drift.
Fully human, drop automation entirely, accept slow and costly.
Split randomly 50/50 with no separation of duties.
Automated continuous regression, with periodic human sprints calibrating the judge.
optionExplanations: 全自动没有人工锚，漂移越积越大且无人纠正，长期不可信。
全人工追不上模型迭代速度，成本线性膨胀，规模上撑不住。
随机对半分不利用各自长处，纯浪费，也没解决漂移校准。
对；自动扛日常回归、人工周期性校准，正好各补对方的短板，可持续又可信。
optionExplanations_en: Fully automated has no human anchor, so drift accumulates uncorrected and becomes untrustworthy long-term.
Fully human can't keep up with model iteration and cost balloons linearly — unscalable.
A random 50/50 split exploits neither's strength and doesn't solve drift calibration.
Correct — automated carries routine regression while periodic human sprints calibrate, each covering the other's weakness, sustainable and trustworthy.

termDefinitions.meaning: 周期性集中投入人力标注一批样本，用于校准自动评估。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An annotation sprint is a periodic concentrated burst of human labeling used to calibrate automated evaluation.

scenario: 除了三元评估的质量分，还想用产品侧信号判断 RAG 系统是否真的帮到了用户。
scenario_en: Beyond the Triad's quality scores, you want product-side signals for whether the RAG system actually helped users.
q: 除了 RAG Triad，哪些是有用的互补产品信号？(多选)
q_en: Beyond the RAG Triad, which are useful complementary product signals? (multiple)
why: task success（用户有没有完成目标）衡量真实价值，escalation rate（拒答/升级频率）暴露系统在哪类查询上没信心。GPU 利用率、BLEU 都不是用户价值信号。
why_en: Task success (did the user accomplish the goal) and escalation rate (how often it refuses/escalates) are product-level signals beyond the Triad, one measuring real value and the other exposing low-confidence query classes.
options: Task success：用户有没有真正完成目标
Escalation rate：系统多频繁拒答或升级到人工
GPU 利用率：服务器算力是否跑满
BLEU 分数：与参考答案的 n-gram 重叠
options_en: Task success: did the user actually accomplish the goal.
Escalation rate: how often it refuses or escalates to a human.
GPU utilization: whether server compute is saturated.
BLEU score: n-gram overlap with a reference answer.
optionExplanations: 对；任务成功率直接衡量系统有没有交付真实价值，是质量分之外的终极信号。
对；拒答/升级频率暴露系统对哪类查询没把握，是有用的补充诊断信号。
错；GPU 利用率是基础设施指标，跟答案是否帮到用户无关。
错；BLEU 盲于幻觉和检索错误，前面已被否定，不是有用的质量信号。
optionExplanations_en: Correct — task success directly measures whether the system delivers real value, the ultimate signal beyond quality scores.
Correct — refusal/escalation frequency exposes which query classes the system is unsure about, a useful diagnostic.
Wrong — GPU utilization is an infrastructure metric, unrelated to whether the answer helped the user.
Wrong — BLEU is blind to hallucination and retrieval errors, already rejected, not a useful quality signal.

termDefinitions.meaning: 系统拒答或把请求转交人工的频率，反映它对某类查询的信心。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Escalation rate is how often the system refuses or hands a request to a human, reflecting its confidence on a query class.

scenario: 检索到的上下文确实切题，但答案里给了一个所有 chunk 都没有的「截止日期」。
scenario_en: The retrieved context is relevant, but the answer states a 'deadline' that appears in none of the chunks.
q: 「检索切题、但答案含一个上下文里没有的截止日期」会被哪些维度抓到？
q_en: Which dimensions catch 'relevant context but an answer stating a deadline absent from all chunks'?
why: 既触发 Faithfulness（答案陈述了上下文不支持的内容 = 幻觉），也触发 Groundedness（那条截止日期主张无法映射到任何 chunk）。Relevance 反而正常，因为检索本身是切题的。
why_en: It trips both Faithfulness (the answer states content the context doesn't support) and Groundedness (the deadline claim maps to no chunk), while Relevance is fine because retrieval was on-topic.
options: 只 Relevance——因为检索环节出了问题
只 Faithfulness——因为这只是文字层面的幻觉，与溯源维度无关
只 Latency——因为响应太快漏掉了事实核对
Faithfulness 与 Groundedness 都会——该主张无法溯源
options_en: Only Relevance — because retrieval is where the problem is.
Only Faithfulness — because this is merely a textual hallucination unrelated to attribution.
Only Latency — because a too-fast response skipped fact checking.
Both Faithfulness and Groundedness — the claim traces back to no chunk.
optionExplanations: 检索是切题的，Relevance 恰恰正常，问题出在生成端。
确实是幻觉，但同一条主张也无法溯源，Groundedness 一样会抓，不止 Faithfulness。
延迟与内容是否有依据无关，答案编日期跟快慢没关系。
对；答案有上下文不支持的内容→Faithfulness 亮红灯，那条日期又映射不到任何段落→Groundedness 也亮。
optionExplanations_en: Retrieval is on-topic, so Relevance is actually fine; the problem is on the generation side.
It is a hallucination, but the same claim is also unattributable, so Groundedness catches it too — not only Faithfulness.
Latency is unrelated to whether content is grounded; inventing a date has nothing to do with speed.
Correct — the answer has unsupported content (Faithfulness flags it) and the date maps to no passage (Groundedness flags it too).

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个失败可能同时触发多个评估维度，据此定位问题在检索还是生成。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cross-dimension diagnosis uses which dimensions a failure trips to locate whether the issue is retrieval or generation.

q: 把「从建评估到持续运营」的 RAG 评估闭环排成正确顺序：
q_en: Order the RAG evaluation lifecycle from building it to continuous operation:
steps: 在留出集上用 LLM 判官做离线回归，每次 pipeline 改动都跑
抽样线上真实流量做异步人工复核，修正反哺判官 prompt 调优
定义带明确锚点的 rubric，人工标注并用 IAA 检查一致性
用达标的人工标签校准并构建 LLM 判官
why: 先立带锚点的 rubric、人工标注并用 IAA 确认可信；再用这些标签校准出 LLM 判官；然后离线每次改动跑回归；最后上线抽样真实流量人工复核，把修正反哺判官调优，闭环。
why_en: First build an anchored rubric with human labels checked by IAA, then calibrate the LLM judge, run offline regression on every change, and finally sample live traffic for human review feeding back into judge tuning.
diagram:
flowchart LR A["rubric+人工标注
IAA 检查"] --> B["校准出
LLM 判官"] B --> C["离线回归
每次改动跑"] C --> D["线上抽样
人工复核"] D --> B

termDefinitions.meaning: 从建 rubric、校准判官、离线回归到在线复核反哺的持续循环。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: The evaluation lifecycle is the continuous loop from building a rubric to calibrating the judge, offline regression, and online review feeding back.
